In all other compounds, Cu ion is present. It has electronic configuration of Cu is [Ar]3d. All electrons are paired.

Hence, they are colourless.

en.explanation:
In [Ni(CO)], Ni is in 0 oxidation state, so there are 8 electrons in 3d subshell and 2 electrons in 4s. CO is the strong ligand, so it cause pairing of electrons in 3d subshell leaving one d subshell vacant. Now, the electron from s shell shifts to d creating vacant space in s subshell and thus the hybridisation is sp.

Ni(28) = [Ar] 4s3d

CO is a strong ligand, causes coupling.

In [Ni(CN)], Ni is in +2 oxidation state so it has 8 electrons in d subshell and CN is also a strong ligand which pairs with d subshell atom and leaves one d orbital empty and thus its hybridisation is dsp.

In [Ni(CN)], the oxidation state of Ni is +2

Ni = [Ar] 3d4s

CN is strong ligand, causes coupling.

en.explanation:
The IUPAC name for [Ni(NH)] [NiCl] is : Tetraamminenickel (II) - tetrachloronickelate (II)

The name of the complex cation is written first followed by the name of the complex anion. Complex cation contains four ammine ligands and complex anion contains four chloride ligands.
